newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Sales gains lift Daily Mail profits.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Sales gains lift Daily Mail profits.

text.p: Strong sales from national titles helped spur a 27 percent rise in underlying half year profit at Daily Mail and General Trust Plc, the British newspaper publisher said on Thursday.

The group, which publishes the Daily Mail and Mail on Sunday newspapers, posted pre-tax profit excluding exceptional items of 46.9 million pounds ($76.6 million) in the six months to end-March, up from 36.9 million.

"Trading conditions in the UK, still the predominant market for the group, remain positive. In these circumstances, the group expects to produce a satisfactory result at the full year," the company said in a statement.
Finance director Peter Williams told Reuters the advertising market appeared fairly strong, particularly recruitment advertising.
The first half figures were towards the bottom end of share analysts' forecasts. Daily Mail shares slipped 2.5p to 17.60 pounds by 1145 GMT on the London Stock Exchange.

Williams said most analysts were focusing on the full-year outlook, rather than the split between the first and second six months. The current consensus estimate is for full year profit before tax of around 125 million pounds. Looking at the newspaper industry generally, Williams noted that Chancellor (Finance Minister) Gordon Brown had pledged not to introduce Value Added Tax on newspapers. The new Labour government will present its first budget on July 2.

The group's flagship Daily Mail newspaper has consolidated its grip on the mid-market sector of the national newspaper business over the past two years. It has boosted sales since Rupert Murdoch's News International closed Today in 1995. The Daily Mail now sells some 2.1 million copies daily, over 900,000 ahead of its mid-market rival The Express.
The group said its newspaper operations, national and local, had benefited from a 15 percent fall in the cost of newsprint -- the raw material for newspapers.
The group reported a 12.4 million pound one-off profit on the sale of its stake in regional broadcaster Westcountry Television to Carlton Communications last December.

The interim dividend was lifted from 4.6 pence to 7.0 pence per share, the size of the rise reflecting an attempt to increase the proportion of the full-year total paid at this stage.($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
